note: One entry per trip round the CRISP-DM cycle. Findings go under the step where they were found. Never rewrite a closed iteration.

iterations.title: Quick, Draw! diamonds are mostly not rhombi
iterations.trigger: A modeling result on validation sent the project back to Data Preparation.
iterations.decision: All Quick, Draw! diamonds excluded by rule before the split; every model retrained.

findings.data: Review sheets showed most Quick, Draw! diamonds are gems, cones, shields or scribbles, which contradicts the class definition.
findings.prep: 500 drawings removed by rule. The split was re-frozen at 12,405 / 2,819 / 2,776.
findings.model: On validation, augmented models rejected those drawings (A1 recall 51 to 59%) while A0 memorized their style (86 to 93%).
findings.eval: Left in, this label noise would have penalized the arms that learn the real shape. Removed before any test read.

iterations.title: Augmentation lost to no augmentation
iterations.trigger: The Stage 5 verdict was fail, and A0, with no augmentation, scored highest. An investigation on train and validation data is running.
iterations.decision: Planned: tune the augmentation and generator on validation, add arm A2 (clean real + augmented real + synthetic), retrain and re-evaluate as a separately reported experiment. The iteration 1 verdict stands.

findings.business: The locked question was B vs A1. The result raises a different question: whether this augmentation design suits these classes at all.
findings.data: A shape's source can be guessed from its pixels (91.7% against 46.7% for the majority guess), so an unaugmented model may lean on dataset style. Whether orientation carries class information is being measured.
findings.prep: Every augmentation and generator range was set by hand and never tested, including rotation of ±180°. A1 and B also never train on an unaugmented image. Measured on validation, three seeds, not on test: with rotation off, A1 reached a mean macro-F1 of 93.15 (92.76, 93.19, 93.49), against 91.69 for A0 and 90.03 for A1 with rotation on. Diamond F1 rose from 83.2 to 96.2.
findings.model: Tuning covered only learning rate and dropout, on A1, and A0 reused A1's winner. A0 stopped at 16 to 24 epochs, while A1 and B mostly ran close to the 30-epoch cap.
findings.eval: Test macro-F1: A0 93.88, A1 90.86, B 90.50. B vs A1 was -0.36, 95% CI [-1.17, 0.41]: fail. Augmentation hurt rectangle, diamond and square, and helped octagon and hexagon. Reading those classes as separated by orientation or proportions versus corner count is a hypothesis under test.
findings.deploy: On drawn shapes, A1 and B can call a square a rectangle while A0 is right. That matches the test pattern but is informal evidence only.
